sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
**Window: the trading week ending 2026-09-04 (the newest SPY bar in every basket and rotation table); cross-asset levels below are the 2026-09-07/08 snapshot noted as such.** The tape this week was quiet at the index but loud underneath: SPY returned essentially flat (+0.1% for the week to 2026-09-04), while rotation ran hard toward hard assets and the physical semiconductor supply chain, and away from software and cybersecurity.

## Ag inputs led everything, on a supply thesis that is not yet confirmed by the price data alone
The El Niño ag basket (DBA, MOS, NTR, DE) was the week's outright leader, +6.6% versus SPY's +0.1% — a +6.5-point one-week excess, on top of +13.3 over four weeks and +11.6 over twelve. That is a real, dated move, not a single-day spike. The mechanism is judgement: an El Niño that tightens grain and soft supply would bid ag inputs, and the theme's stated evidence (NOAA ONI ≥ +0.5 for three consecutive months; CBOT front-month vs 20-day) is operator-checked, not something the return series proves. Counterevidence to keep honest: the theme was only entered 2026-09-06, so its since-entry excess is 0.0% — the 6.5-point number is trailing beta into the position, not performance of the call. Relative strength alone does not identify weather as the cause.

## The semi supply chain split cleanly by layer
Within our own sector map the dispersion was the story. Memory/Storage led at +7.6% (STX, WDC, MU, SNDK, 4 of 4 higher vs SPY) and Foundry +5.4% (INTC, TSEM, TSM, UMC, 4 of 4). Computer/GPU added +3.4% and Semi-Logic/ASIC +1.8%. But Semi-Cap/EDA lagged at −1.5% (8 of 8 below SPY) — the tools-and-design layer did not participate. That divergence — physical capacity and memory bid, capital-equipment fading — is the notable internal fact; I won't assign it a single cause without the order and utilization data that would support one. XLK itself was only +0.9% for the week (+0.7 excess), so the semiconductor strength was concentrated, not a broad tech bid.

## Software and cyber were the funding source
The other side of the rotation: Cybersecurity −6.9% (NET, S, CRWD, PANW, 4 of 4 below SPY) and Software/SaaS −4.7% (6 of 6) were the worst sector rows on the board. Cloud/Hyperscaler was roughly flat-to-down at −1.3%. At the ETF level XLY (−2.0%, −2.1 excess) and XLI (−1.1%, and −5.0 over four weeks) were the laggards; XLV (+0.2% week, +7.9% over twelve) and XLF (+9.3% over twelve) hold the longer-horizon leadership. This is a market rotating out of long-duration growth and into value/defensive and physical assets.

## Rates and vol were calm; the Fed is the live variable
Cross-asset confirmation was muted. The 10-year sat at 4.788% and the 2-year at 4.375% (both 2026-09-07/08 snapshots, ~flat on the day); the 2s10s curve at 41.3 bp. High-yield spreads tightened a touch to 2.65% (as of 2026-09-03) — no stress signal. VIX at 14.52 is low. The one genuinely unusual macro fact: the 9/16 FOMC path prices a 57.9% HIKE probability (as of 2026-09-07), with 12/9 at 54% HIKE. A market pricing a coin-flip-plus toward a September hike, while equities sit flat and vol sits at 14, is the tension worth watching. Unusual Whales' 2026-09-08T00:03:48Z wire noted markets pricing "~60% odds of a Fed hike next week" alongside gold near $4,400 and Mideast supply risk — consistent with the hike-and-inflation read, though a headline is a citation, not evidence of positioning.

## Commodities backdrop
Gold held ~$4,421 (−0.19% snapshot) and WTI crude firmed toward $92 (+0.83% snapshot), with the oil bid tied in the same-day wire (2026-09-08T00:23:19Z) to reported strikes on a Saudi Aramco refinery and Hormuz shipping tension. Firm crude plus a firm hike bet is the inflationary combination that keeps the front end pinned.

Limitation: the reports feed carried no close-phase market observations for most of this week (only 2026-09-03 held a candidate; 2026-09-04 close was empty), so the dated narrative rests on the rotation and frame tables rather than day-by-day notes.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
The coming week's single pivot is the 2026-09-16 FOMC, which prices a 57.9% hike probability. That is close enough to a coin flip that either outcome moves rates and, by extension, the growth-vs-value rotation that defined this week. The observable that matters is the front end: the 2-year (4.375%) and the hike odds themselves. If the odds firm above ~60%, expect the software/cyber underperformance and the value/defensive bid to persist, since a hike is the direct headwind to long-duration multiples. If the odds fade toward a hold, the reverse risk is a sharp mean-reversion snapback in the beaten-down Software/SaaS and Cybersecurity rows — the two worst sectors this week are also the most rate-sensitive to reprice.

The ag-input leadership is the week's most extended move and therefore the most exposed. It can persist only if the supply thesis keeps getting confirmed — the theme's own kill condition is ONI < +0.5 two months running, or a 10% underperformance over 60 sessions; neither is met. But a +6.5-point weekly excess after +13.3 over four weeks invites a pullback on any grain-price reversal or a risk-on rotation back into growth. Watch CBOT corn/wheat front-month versus the 20-day as the confirming tell; a break below would remove the mechanism.

The semiconductor supply-chain split is the structural theme to track. The question is whether Memory/Storage (+7.6%) and Foundry (+5.4%) leadership broadens back into Semi-Cap/EDA (−1.5%), or whether the tools layer keeps lagging — the latter would argue the memory/foundry move is a pricing/utilization event rather than a new capex cycle. The nearest scheduled read-through is distant (ASML 2026-10-14, CDNS 2026-10-26), so this resolves on price and any interim orders/utilization data, not on an earnings print next week.

ADBE reports post-market 2026-09-10, the only single-name catalyst inside seven days, with a 6.93% implied move and IV rank 68.84 — the market is pricing a real event. Software/SaaS is the week's second-worst sector, so ADBE prints into a weak tape and a stretched policy backdrop; the read there will color sentiment on the whole SaaS complex.

Reverse risk to the whole framing: rates are calm (VIX 14.52, HY 2.65%, curve 41.3 bp), so the market is not braced for a hawkish surprise. A hike delivered into that complacency is the asymmetric risk; a dovish hold into this rotation is the mirror-image squeeze.
